newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says 1996 inflation target at 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says 1996 inflation target at 8.7 pct.

text.p: The Philippine government has revised upward its inflation target for the year to an average of 8.7 percent from 8.5 due to the increases in domestic oil prices and the increased consumer spending during Christmas, Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said on Tuesday.
Inflation is also expected quicken due to Christmas spending in the fourth quarter this year, he said.
From a low of 4.4 percent in September, "it (inflation) will accelerate in October to more than five percent and probably end the year at 6.0 to 6.5 percent," Habito told reporters.
Inflation was at double-digit levels since the start of the year. It later tapered down to a single-digit level in June.
Since August this year, the government adopted an automatic oil pricing mechanism to pave the way for full deregulation of the local petroleum industry by March 1997.
Petroleum prices increased by an average of 6.96 centavos per litre in September and further by 30.72 centavos in October.
